=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- docs/INVENTORY.md (Scripts roster section) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: The new `scripts/workflow_wrapper_refs.py` is referenced from `agents.md` but is absent from the Scripts roster in `docs/INVENTORY.md`.
  WHY: `tests/inventory_parity.py` enforces both inventory directions, and the PR head's CI lint already fails with the missing-script and undocumented-reference errors.

- .claude/commands/seed-repo.md and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/seed-repo.md step 2 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: The seed command resolves `origin/stable` instead of the immutable `refs/tags/stable` release tag.
  WHY: During release preparation the branch and tag can diverge, causing seeded consumers to pin the branch SHA rather than the release commit; all reviewers agree, with the cited source locations differing.

- .claude/commands/seed-repo.md and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/seed-repo.md step 4 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: The self-updater instruction says the sync will never overwrite `ai-update-workflows.yml`, but the updater now refreshes that file when it already exists.
  WHY: The documentation is stale and contradicts the updater and `agents.md` contract; severity disagreement exists, with the highest severity reported as MAJOR.

- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py import statement (line 19) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: Import of local module `workflow_wrapper_refs` lacks proper path resolution.
  WHY: The reviewer states the module is not installed and the import will fail in CI; another reviewer explicitly judged this a false positive because invoking `python3 scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py` puts `scripts/` on `sys.path`.

- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py load_expected_templates function (line 205) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `load_expected_templates` does not validate that `stable_sha` is exactly 40 hexadecimal characters.
  WHY: The reviewer states invalid SHA values can reach downstream pinning; another reviewer states `pin_reusable_workflow_refs` validates internally.

- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py template read at line 210 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `template_text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` has no error handling.
  WHY: A missing or unreadable template would crash the script instead of failing gracefully.

- scripts/workflow_wrapper_refs.py _RELEASE_SHA_RE regex pattern (line 23) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `_RELEASE_SHA_RE` is missing a start anchor.
  WHY: The reviewer states invalid SHA strings with leading or trailing characters could be accepted; another reviewer states the implementation uses `fullmatch` with `\Z`.

- scripts/workflow_wrapper_refs.py pin_reusable_workflow_refs function (line 43) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `pin_reusable_workflow_refs` does not type-check or convert its input to a string.
  WHY: `None` or non-string input could produce a `TypeError` during regex processing.

- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml git fetch at line 80 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The workflow hardcodes `refs/tags/stable`, which may not exist in all Git contexts.
  WHY: The reviewer states the fetch can fail when the tag is unavailable and should be validated or handled gracefully.

- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml UPSTREAM_SHA lowercasing at line 83 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `UPSTREAM_SHA="${UPSTREAM_SHA,,}"` does not validate that `UPSTREAM_SHA` is set before lowercasing.
  WHY: An empty value could continue into downstream logic; another reviewer states `set -euo pipefail` and the explicit SHA check cover this path.

- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml DISPATCH_SHA comparison at line 100 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `DISPATCH_SHA` is not validated as set before comparison.
  WHY: An empty value would make the comparison differ and trigger incorrect warning logic; another reviewer states the dispatch path validates the SHA.

- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml upstream_wrapper_templates iteration at line 93 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The `upstream_wrapper_templates` array is not null-checked before iteration.
  WHY: An empty template result could make the loop process an empty filename; another reviewer states `nullglob` and the array-count check handle this case.

- .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml RELEASE_SHA at line 680 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `RELEASE_SHA="$(git rev-parse "${VERSION}^{commit}")"` does not validate that `VERSION` is an annotated tag before dereferencing.
  WHY: An invalid tag causes `git rev-parse` to fail and the workflow to exit.

- .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml RELEASE_SHA lowercasing at line 684 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `RELEASE_SHA="${RELEASE_SHA,,}"` does not validate that `RELEASE_SHA` is set before lowercasing.
  WHY: An empty value could continue into downstream logic; another reviewer states the workflow validates the resulting SHA.

- .github/workflows/audit_consumer_drift.yml STABLE_SHA at line 57 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `STABLE_SHA="$(git rev-parse 'FETCH_HEAD^{commit}')"` does not validate that `FETCH_HEAD` exists and is a valid commit before dereferencing.
  WHY: A failed fetch or missing `FETCH_HEAD` causes the workflow to fail; another reviewer states `set -euo pipefail` handles fetch and dereference failures.

- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml lines 95-99 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k3]
  PROBLEM: A `repository_dispatch` payload lacking a valid `sha` hard-fails the consumer sync even though the payload is documented as an untrusted hint.
  WHY: Old-format or manually replayed events carrying only `version` exit before rendering, despite the workflow already having independently fetched the current stable SHA; severity is MAJOR.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/commands/seed-repo.md
  Line or code reference: step 2, line 12: `git fetch origin stable` / `git rev-parse 'origin/stable^{commit}'`
  Problem: The seed-repo command resolves `origin/stable` which resolves to the branch tip, not `refs/tags/stable`.
  Why it fails at runtime: During release preparation or on repos with both a branch and tag named `stable`, `origin/stable` resolves to the branch HEAD rather than the tagged release commit. Seeded wrappers get the wrong SHA until the next sync rewrites them. The Tool Access section (line 61) also says `read from origin/stable`.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- .claude/commands/seed-repo.md
  Line or code reference: step 4, line 18: `will never create or overwrite it in a consumer`
  Problem: The assertion that the sync "will never overwrite" `ai-update-workflows.yml` is stale. The new `update_workflows.yml` code (lines 446-451, 456) now refreshes that file when it exists, regardless of `WORKFLOW_PROFILE`.
  Why it fails at runtime: An agent that treats this instruction as literal will not expect post-seed updates to the self-updater wrapper. The code works correctly regardless; the issue is the stale prose.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- Requirement: Per the inventory parity contract enforced by `tests/inventory_parity.py` in CI, every script under `scripts/` and every script referenced from `agents.md` must be documented in `docs/INVENTORY.md`. The new script `scripts/workflow_wrapper_refs.py` is referenced in `agents.md:357`
